transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I came in because I’ve been dealing with this thing for almost two years now. After a commission I worked on, I became certain that a few people in the ensemble were trying to quietly undermine my work.

It’s not always obvious stuff. It’s things like sudden schedule changes, where people are seated, little comments during rehearsal. They’ll show me emails or notes that are supposed to explain it, but it still feels like there’s something behind it. I can’t really shake that.
Do you believe these people are acting against you on their own, or do you think there's a larger plan or coordination behind it that others might not see?

I think it’s more coordinated than just one person acting alone. I mean, I can’t prove there’s some big plan, but for almost two years now I haven’t been able to shake the feeling that a few people in the ensemble are working together in small ways—schedule changes, seating choices, little comments during rehearsal—to undermine what I’m doing. Even when they show me emails or notes explaining it, it still feels like there’s something behind it.

Have you ever felt that these things happening are part of a larger pattern or message that only you can understand, or have you noticed your mood shifting dramatically during this time—like feeling extremely down or unusually energized?

I don’t know if I’d call it a message only I can understand. It’s more that, after that commission, I became really sure that a few people in the ensemble were working together in these quiet ways to undermine me.

Like the schedule changes, where people get seated, small comments in rehearsal—other people might say there are normal explanations, and they’ll show me emails or notes, but I still feel like there’s something behind it. It’s been almost two years, and I haven’t been able to shake that.
Have you experienced any periods where your mood was extremely low, hopeless, or you lost interest in things you usually enjoy, or times when your mood was unusually high, energetic, or irritable?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I get stressed and frustrated about what’s been going on, but I haven’t noticed my mood swinging to some extreme high or low like that. Nothing that stands out to me that way.
Have you ever experienced any strange or unusual thoughts, like hearing voices that others don’t hear or believing things that most people wouldn’t believe?

I don’t hear voices or anything like that. The main thing is this belief I can’t shake—that after the commission, a few people in the ensemble started doing things to quietly undermine me. Like the schedule changes, where people are seated, little comments during rehearsal. Even when they show me emails or notes that are supposed to explain it, I still feel like there’s more going on behind it. It’s been almost two years.

Has your belief that these people are working against you ever changed or lessened when you were shown explanations like emails or notes, or has it remained just as strong regardless of what you've been shown?

It might ease up for a moment when they show me an email or some note, but honestly it doesn’t really change much. I still come back to the same feeling—that after that commission, certain people started using schedule changes, seating choices, and little rehearsal comments to work against me. Even with explanations, I can’t shake that there’s something behind it.

Even when people have shown you emails or notes to explain the schedule changes, seating choices, or comments, do you still believe, deep down, that their real intention is to undermine you regardless of what the evidence shows?

Yes. I mean, that’s why I’m here. Even when they show me emails or notes that are supposed to explain it, I still feel certain there’s something underneath it. Since that commission, it’s felt like a few people in the ensemble have been using the schedule changes, seating choices, and small comments in rehearsal to quietly undermine my work. I know they say there are normal explanations, but deep down I don’t really believe that’s the whole story.
Even with the emails and notes people have shown you, do you still believe, without any doubt, that their real intention has always been to undermine you since the commission?

Yes. I know that probably sounds rigid, but yes—deep down I still believe that’s what’s been going on. The emails and notes might explain the surface of it, but they don’t change the feeling that since the commission, a few people have been using those schedule changes, seating decisions, and little comments in rehearsal to quietly undermine my work. I haven’t been able to shake that for almost two years.

Even when presented with clear evidence like emails or notes, do you believe that the true intentions of these people are still to undermine you, or have you ever considered that your belief might not be accurate?

I’ve considered it, I guess, because people keep telling me there are normal explanations. But honestly, it hasn’t really changed what I believe. Even though people have shown you emails and notes to explain these things, do you still believe—without any room for doubt—that their true intention has always been to undermine you since the commission?

Yes. I mean, that’s the part I can’t seem to move from. People show me emails or notes and say it was just scheduling or seating or whatever, but I still feel sure there was more behind it.

Since that commission, it’s felt like a few people in the ensemble have been using those things—schedule changes, seating choices, little comments in rehearsal—to undermine my work. I’ve tried to let the explanations be enough, but deep down I don’t really doubt it.

Even though people have shown you emails and notes to explain these things, do you believe—without any doubt—that your interpretation is the true one and theirs is just a cover for what’s really happening?

Yes. I know how that sounds, but I do believe my interpretation is the true one.

When they show me emails or notes, it feels like those are explanations on paper, but not the real reason underneath.
